title: "What if Larian had shut down after Divine Divinity?": Star Trek Online exec scorns publishers who close teams like BioWare in favour of "AAA veteran" start-ups and AI "magic beans"
description: Breaking up established game development teams in favour of "AAA veteran" start-ups and "magic bean" technologies is like "setting fire to millions of dollars of property and equipment", in the words of Star Trek Online executive producer Thomas Marrone. He thinks it's "wildly irresponsible and self-sabotaging", and that videogame company shareholders should be absolutely furious about it. Marrone's comments come in response to EA closing BioWare yesterday, but he takes aim at closures and layoffs across the industry. He notes that many of the most successful teams owe their accomplishments to lessons learned from screw-ups, and suggests that if big game publishers just want "number to go up", they should get out of the game-making trade and pour all their cash into investment funds. Read more

title: How Will Gas And Refueling Work In GTA 6?
description: As more Grand Theft Auto 6 previews roll out, one topic seems to be proving pretty controversial among fans--the realistic need to refuel your vehicle. Some players think it's a little egregious of Rockstar to force you to hunt down gasoline, while others consider that because of the game's other realistic mechanisms--like relationships, working out, and escaping the police --that needing to refuel should have been introduced to the franchise a long while back. While the details aren't concrete right now, we know there will be at least two types of cars--ones that need gasoline and electric vehicles. There may be some hybrid vehicles, but it hasn't been confirmed just yet. You'll have to charge electric cars, of course, but we know more about how fueling a vehicle works. It seems to be a quick time event (QTE) that lasts around 10 seconds. You'll have to hold the gas pump, hold R2 or RB, and pump gas until the car is full. However, there's more of a risk if you've stolen a car--if you want to get away but you have to take a detour to a gas station because you're running out of fuel, it will be less than ideal. That's made even more difficult if you're sporting a Wanted level for stealing it in the first place. This will change the way we behave with our vehicles throughout the entire game. It seems like Rockstar wants you to care about the vehicle you have, rather than in previous instalments where there was no incentive to look after your car. You'd just see a new vehicle, ditch your current one, and steal that instead. If you've just spent some hard-earned cash on filling it with gas so that it's a reliable getaway vehicle, you're going to be far less likely to ditch it. Filling a car with gas has existed basically since cars have been in games, prominently in racing games where you'd have to pull over to refuel, or more recently in simulation games like My Summer Car, The Long Drive, and more. In our accompanying video above, you'll see that at this point…

title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Tips For Multiplayer
description: We went hands-on with Modern Warfare 4 early, and while it will feel familiar to many Call of Duty veterans, Infinity Ward has updated some of the movement mechanics and features from recent years. In this guide, we'll provide some of the best tips to help you score wins in multiplayer when Modern Warfare 4 launches on October 23. Practice the new movement Modern Warfare 4 overhauls the movement from the last two years of Treyarch's Black Ops games. This game strips away the fancy omnimovement, but Infinity Ward has reworked the mantling system, refined the sliding mechanic, and added a way to climb up pipes. The best way to get practice with Modern Warfare 4's movement system is to play the game's new mobility course, which is found in the multiplayer playlist menu. It includes a series of three difficulties, including tutorials for beginners, intermediate, and experts. There are rewards for completing the mobility course as well. Without omnimovement, double jumps into windows and other high places are no longer possible. However, you can climb up pipes to reach otherwise inaccessible areas. These specific pipes are copper in color and stand out fairly easily. These are found on standard multiplayer maps, Kill Block, and even Modern Warfare 4's Zodiac map for Warzone. Hipfire is your friend Infinity Ward removed bloom from guns this year, which is a mechanic that previously caused bullet spread when firing from the hip, meaning some bullets did not hit their target. Hipfiring is more accurate in Modern Warfare 4, so you don't always need to aim down sights with your gun. If someone is sliding at you from around a corner, or perhaps you just find yourself in a close-range engagement. Don't waste time aiming. Just hipfire your gun. Adjust your settings Modern Warfare 4 has plenty of customization and accessibility settings. These include options to help make the game's movement easier, refine your aiming, and help with issues like Tinnitus or motion sickness.…

title: To Start The New Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners 2 Quest, Do These Two Things First
description: Cyberpunk 2077 may have come out six years ago, but developer CD Projekt RED has just released a new update. The 2.5 patch adds a plethora of fixes and features, and it's also themed after Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2, including a themed quest and rewards to boot. The Edgerunners 2 mission is called Clampdown, and it serves as a prequel of sorts to the events of the anime's new season. It features character King and his crew, and thankfully, it has no spoilers for the actual show. Rather, it serves as an extension, further tying the Cyberpunk transmedia efforts with each other. Depending on the progress you've made in the game, though, you may not automatically gain access to Clampdown. If you're wondering how to start the Edgerunners 2 mission Cyberpunk 2077 so you can dive straight into it and reap the new rewards, we've got you covered. In This Article How to Start Clampdown, The Edgerunners 2 Mission in Cyberpunk 2077 Where to Find Wakako Gig Locations in Cyberpunk 2077 Rewards for the Edgerunners 2 Mission in Cyberpunk 2077 How to Start Clampdown, The Edgerunners 2 Mission in Cyberpunk 2077 Upon downloading the 2.5 update and booting up the game, Clampdown isn't immediately available. Rather, there are two steps you need to tackle. First, you must ensure that you've finished The Heist. This is part of the main questline, and essentially serves as the culmination of the first act of the story. As such, you'll naturally get to it. Make sure to fully finish it. Then, you must complete at least two gigs with Wakako. Once you're done, you'll have to wait to receive a text message from her. I skipped time for 24 hours, and then for 12 hours, and the message was on my phone right after. You may need to actually open your phone to see it, however. Keep an eye out from a text from Wakako, not a call. This last step can be tricky. Gigs are everywhere on the map, but you never get an indication about who they correspond to until you get close to them. Depending on what…

title: BioWare Did Something Very Rare For The Time: It Took Star Wars Seriously
description: In what seemed to be an inevitability, Electronic Arts announced the closure of BioWare this week, including the cancellation of its current project, a future iteration in the Mass Effect series. The writing has been on the wall for some time, and EA's recent sale to Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) sealed its fate. Much can (and should) be said about BioWare's ability to create fully realized, original worlds like those of Mass Effect and Dragon Age. But to write the developer's epitaph, we also have to recognize the incredible job it did as the steward of one of the most popular franchises in the world. BioWare truly understood Star Wars, down to its very bones, and that knowledge resulted in one of the best Star Wars games of all time. I barely even need to mention that I'm referring to Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. The hit from BioWare was its breakout success, remembered for its rich RPG mechanics and a twist that felt mind-blowing at the time. Without it, we may not have ever gotten modern classics like The Witcher 3, to say nothing of BioWare's own Mass Effect and Dragon Age titles. Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic The creators of Knights of the Old Republic had the vision to set it in a new era of Star Wars, thousands of years before the events of the original movie, separating its story from the main continuity of films that has become a crutch for lots of modern Star Wars stories both in and outside of games. The Old Republic setting was a bold new direction, allowing fans to see the height of the Jedi Order decades before Disney introduced the High Republic era. The worldbuilding was so rich and seamless, in fact, that even though KOTOR itself has fallen out of official Star Wars canon, many parts have been borrowed and adapted into modern Star Wars lore. Memorable additions like deadly HK droids, the barren planet Malachor, the broad outlines of the Mandalorian War, and even the existence of Darth Revan have become canonized…

description: We've had about roughly four decades of games as we generally know them now, and yet somehow, so often their stories feel so limited in scope. I'm not talking about a lack of big, bold ideas, in fact there might be too many of those. I more mean that there are aspects to life that often go uncovered in games. For example, when was the last time you saw a game about a workers strike? Citizen Sleeper 2 has one questline about such a thing, but it's just what the entire game is about. A Line Held Tight, a mecha visual novel about a sci-fi miner's strike, may bridge that gap. Read more

title: After The BioWare Shutdown, Mass Effect Spiritual Successor Exodus Gets A New Look
description: In the wake of the news that EA has closed down BioWare and ended development on Mass Effect 5, Archetype Entertainment—co-founded by former BioWare devs Chad Robertson, James Ohlen, and Drew Karpyshyn—has given players a brand-new look at its upcoming title, a very Mass-Effecty sci-fi RPG called Exodus. Specifically, Archetype has revealed a visual rework of its male player-character model. When GameSpot previewed Exodus in late August, the male version of protagonist Jun Aslan could be seen sporting a five-o'-clock shadow and very different bone structure. Now, he has a whole new face. In a new video uploaded to Archetype's YouTube channel today, Archetype general manager Chad Robertson showed off male-Jun's new look, which he explained is a result of player feedback. "We've seen your conversations and feedback over the last few months around our male Jun character model," Robertson said. "We've been listening, and we take that feedback seriously. We've continued to refine Jun as we've worked on him and the rest of the game." Archetype hasn't yet revealed Jun's female character model, but the devs say her reveal is on the way. "Is FemJun on your mind?" a new post on the official Exodus website asks. "Ours too! And we’re happy to say yes, she’s coming... soon™. We’ve got something special cooking for her reveal, and we think it’ll be worth the wait." Exodus launches on April 7, 2027 and is available to wishlist now on the PlayStation Store, Xbox Store, Steam, and the Epic Games Store.

title: EA Has A New Plan For Madden, And It Leans Into Everything The Company Gets Wrong
description: Electronic Arts is developing an American football experience unlike anything it's made before, the company said in a memo shared publicly after closing BioWare and laying off 400 people across the company. In trying to spin the news positively and toward the future, the memo's attributed writers, chief studios officer Cam Weber and chief operating officer David Tinson, spoke about several of the publishing giant's upcoming games, including something EA is calling Project Gridiron. What is Project Gridiron? The memo's exact phrasing calls it a "social-first open-world experience for our American Football team." In other words, EA is getting closer to something I've been writing about for years: Madden (and possibly College Football) heavily cribbing from NBA 2K's The City mode and giving football fans a virtual social space of their own. The memo speaks of Project Gridiron as a glimmering future prospect, ignoring--or perhaps unaware of--the fact that such a mode requires EA to be a totally different company than it has proven to be. A mode like The City demands three things the EA Sports brand has historically lacked: patience, an authentic voice, and community goodwill. In NBA 2K, The City is a social hub that players can jump into with friends and strangers. In this open-world setting, players play pick-up streetball games and limited-time modes, enter tournaments for prizes, work out, practice, or simply cross the virtual hangout space to get to their next NBA game in their custom avatar's solo career. Importantly, it's also dominated by spending opportunities, including in-game shops that sell sneakers from brands such as Nike and Adidas, streetwear from labels like Fried Rice and Washed Dads, fantasy items like magician and dragon costumes, as well as branded watches, arm sleeves, sunglasses, scooters, and much more. As rich as it is with things to do, it's also packed with ways to spend money. EA's gamble with its marquee sports games demands it behaves like…

title: GTA 6’s New TV Trailer Is A Bit Different, See It For Yourself
description: GTA 6 's marketing push is ramping up substantially, and that includes with TV commercials. Eagled-eyes fans have discovered that the new GTA 6 TV spots actually contain some extended sequences, but just barely. For starters, a 30-second TV spot cuts out the steamy shower scenes with Jason and Lucia from the launch trailer. While the shower scenes are gone in this edit, the new TV spot has a slightly longer shots of an airplane sequence and another with Jason and Lucia standing next to their car. Jason playfully nudges Lucia, and in the TV spot, she nearly topples to the ground. The Xbox logo was also removed, presumably due to Rockstar's reported promotional deal with Sony. You can check out the comparison below ( via IGN ). A 90-second version, meanwhile, includes the shower scenes, along with the slightly longer sequences seen in the 30-second version. If you saw these TV spots recently, you might not have even noticed any of these changes, but GTA 6 fan accounts are extremely dedicated and never miss anything. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and, yes, Xbox Series X|S, even though the TV ads for the game don't tell you that. Rockstar's marketing push for the game also includes real-life Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell restaurants where you can buy GTA-branded food. In other GTA 6 news, it was recently reported that preorders are pacing significantly ahead of any other big AAA game of the past five years. Obviously that's no surprise, given GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest game release ever, and it could generate $2 billion before it even launches.

title: I’m Getting Very Worried About Skate Following EA Layoffs
description: Publisher Electronic Arts recently slashed 400 roles across its company, which resulted in the shuttering of legendary RPG studio BioWare. But also impacted by the layoffs was Skate developer Full Circle, and now I'm growing increasingly worried about the future of a franchise I waited so long to make a comeback. Part of EA's latest round of layoffs on October 21 included cutting an unspecified number of staffers to create a "very clear roadmap" that leads to a "healthier and more sustainable business." Then, as VGC noted on the same day, "many" of the developers at Full Circle are gone. This includes artists Brendan Vermeltfoort and Will Granda, seasonal creative director John Epler, and senior designers Adam Martinazzi and David Milne--all of whom posted the unfortunate news on LinkedIn. It's always a bummer when talented developers lose their jobs at the hands of corporate greed, but this one stings for me personally. As a big Skate girlie, I was so stoked for the franchise to make a comeback, and even more stoked to get my hands on the game in September 2025. It's had its stumbles, to be sure. Season 2 was light on new content. Season 3 introduced a new map... that was locked behind a paywall. Season 4 gave us an empty stadium... that was also locked behind a paywall. But despite bailing on every trick, you could see Full Circle getting closer to landing at each attempt. Season 5, which kicked off on September 8, hasn't been the best, but it has been a solid step in the right direction, and even came with a massive park reminiscent of Skate 3 's Super Ultra Mega Park. Along the way, there have been new tricks, new attempts at progression (that oftentimes drew the ire of the player base), a smattering of new gear, and a plethora of bug fixes to make each season a bit smoother than the last (though there were inevitably bugs with each new content drop). It was evident that Full Circle, which is composed of developers who worked on the entire Skate franchise,…

title: It Isn’t Debra Wilson’s Fault She’s In Everything
description: Debra Wilson’s voice, one of the most recognizable in video games, carries a singular authority. It’s a sound that’s propped up special agents, presidents, military commanders, dragons, demons, and Jedi masters. But despite her incredible range--Wolfenstein cutscene director Tom Keegan calls her "his muse" because he loves to work with her so much--she’s also one of gaming's most recognizable faces. Game developers often scan her and build characters around her commanding presence, individuality, and unmistakable aura. It’s a blessing and a curse for an actor who wants to inhabit characters. Wilson has voiced main characters in over 100 different games, but there is also at least a double-digit number of games in which the creators have used her physical likeness, as well. "I don’t necessarily dig it," Wilson told GameSpot in an exclusive interview. "Because I might as well be doing it on camera. It's hard to suspend your disbelief. There are people who are like, ‘Oh my God, she's in every f***ing game. What the f***?’ And there are other people like, ‘I am sick of looking at her face because I just want to play the game and not think of Debra Wilson.’" Recently, Wilson’s prominence in games was parodied in Focus M, an internet video poking fun at AAA game design. The video sees Mario running around a horrifically generic fan-made Unreal Engine-style world, quipping and being guided by a voice on the radio. The big reveal at the end shows Wilson in her home booth, as the voice behind Toadsworth. While it suggests she’s in on the joke, unfortunately--like her Destiny 2 farewell video --it just came in as a request on Cameo, a service where fans pay actors to record lines in character. She’d never seen the video until I showed it to her, though she said she loved it. Wilson does her best to remain unplugged from the discourse, but it still sometimes spills over into her periphery and she sees the comments from people who say they’re sick of seeing her face pop up in…

title: WoW: Forever Is Keeping Its Secrets Close To The Chest
description: World of Warcraft: Forever players may have searched its beta with a fine-toothed comb, but Blizzard said there are still plenty of secrets waiting to be found come launch and beyond. In a new WoW: Forever Podcast dedicated to the end of the beta, Blizzard made clear it's keeping many of the game's surprises close to its chest. Senior game designer Josh Greenfield said Blizzard had disabled some items and secrets for the beta. He gave an example of a new torch item that was originally turned off for the beta's first week, but later enabled to test out Forever's new lighting and fog tech. He said players can expect more of those types of surprises. "There's definitely some secrets and stuff that we had turned off," Greenfield said when asked about still to be discovered secrets in the level 1-30 zones. "There's going to be things to discover that we didn't surface, suffice to say that." Forever's beta had a maximum level of 30, meaning there is still a huge chunk of the game, including new zones, quests, dungeons, and raids, players haven't fully explored yet. When asked about items like a newly discovered sword in the beta that could potentially enable new playstyles, like a melee-focused "Battle Mage", Greenfield opted not to elaborate further. "It's hard to talk about secret stuff," Greenfield said. "It's secret, right? We want people to find it. There's some really, really, really cool, and really, really, really well-buried stuff out there that's probably going to take people a long time to find. If we tip our hats to it too much, it's just going to take the fun away." Unlike in past WoW releases, most of the items on Forever's beta were hidden from dataminers using a new system that hides an item's name and stats until it's discovered by the community. At the start of the beta, over 12,500 items were kept hidden. As a result, players don't know what items drop from dungeon bosses or what some of the best quest rewards are. The game is still a mystery,…

title: The Leaked Mass Effect 5 Trailer Is Absolutely Heartbreaking
description: After hearing the disappointing news that EA has shuttered BioWare, putting an end to two of my favorite RPG franchises— Mass Effect and Dragon Age —I have been, like so many other players, feeling pretty bummed out. But I consoled myself with the fact that, given the environment at BioWare in recent years, the now-canceled Mass Effect 5 probably wouldn't be that good anyway. Like many players, I enjoyed the Mass Effect trilogy, but felt that Mass Effect: Andromeda fell short. Similarly, BioWare's other recent titles— Anthem and Dragon Age: The Veilguard —struggled with messy development cycles marked by frequent changes in direction, mixed messages from higher-ups at EA, constant staff turnover, and other issues that ultimately led to an underwhelming gaming experience. After playing Veilguard, which felt nothing like the Dragon Age games I had grown to love, my hopes weren't too high for Mass Effect 5. The news of its cancellation (and BioWare's subsequent shutdown) was a huge bummer, though I'd rather Mass Effect go out on a relatively high note than see it get the Veilguard treatment. But then I saw the trailer. Uploaded to Reddit earlier today, the trailer has not been verified as real by BioWare, but it doesn't appear to bear any hallmarks of generative AI, and a short message before the trailer begins implies it was planned to debut at a later date—perhaps N7 Day, or The Game Awards. "The following is in-engine footage from our small team," reads the text displayed before the trailer begins. "It uses our pre-production assets." What follows is one of the most exciting game trailers I've seen in years. We learn the name of the game—Mass Effect: Universe—and meet the male version of its protagonist (though given the history of the franchise, it's likely players would have been able to play as whatever gender they prefer). This nameless protagonist is in a bar, flirting heavily with an Asari. After some additional romantic banter, our protagonist explains that…

title: Why People Think Valve Just Accidentally Confirmed Half-Life 3
description: People online are going wild thinking that Valve may have accidentally revealed the existence of a new Half-Life game after a developer mentioned a project referred to as "HLX." Speaking at the Game Sound Con event, Valve sound designer Mike Morasky was discussing how Valve's games utilize high dynamic range (HDR) audio systems. He specifically called out how upcoming Valve game Deadlock has its own version of HDR and so does a project called HLX. Another Valve developer sitting next to Morasky says to him immediately after, "Nice work," seemingly in reference to how Morasky might have spoken out of turn here by mentioning HLX. You can also see the other Valve developer saying to Morasky, "Good job, you only said HLX once." Morasky is a Valve veteran, having worked on the sound and music for games like Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead, Portal 2, Half-Life: Alyx, and Counter-Strike 2. Outside of games, he worked on visual effects for Peter Jackson's The Lord of the Rings movies and The Matrix trilogy. He was a member of the band Steel Pole Bath Tab. A while back, a datamining effort found references to something called HLX, and some think it's a new Half-Life game, or possibly the fabled Half-Life 3. For what it's worth, it's become something of an annual tradition for people to get excited about the smallest possible evidence of a new Half-Life, only to be disappointed when nothing gets announced. The Half-Life franchise has a dedicated fanbase and the franchise has major cache, so it wouldn't be surprising to see Valve return to the series again after 2020's VR game Half-Life: Alyx. That was GameSpot's Game of the Year that year.

title: Captivating cosmic megastructure adventure game Hypnos leaves early access next week, offering up a world I'm desperate to dig into further
description: I just love me a megastructure, I do. I'm not entirely sure why, to be honest. My best guess is that growing up in a major city with concrete pillars looming over me higher into the sky than I care to take notice of, perhaps even threatening me, left me with a sense of awe towards that which exists at a scale I can't really comprehend. With that, I was quite quickly hooked on whatever Hypnos was putting down, even if when I first had a go at it I couldn't quite tell you what was going on. And now, after a stint in early access, the eldritch "megastructure fever dream," is launching into 1.0 in just a week's time! Read more
